title: Proteome Profiling Among Aging Cell Lines
projectDescription: Characterization of the proteome provides direct information on disease-associated pathways during the onset and progression of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). In this project, we employed high-resolution mass spectrometry to quantify the proteomes of AD cell cultures using multiplexed quantification. The following phenotypes were measured: Control (Nt), lamin A mutation (La), progerin (Pg), classical AD mutation (AppNt), AD mutation with lamin A (AppLa), and AD mutation with progerin (AppPg).
sampleProcessingProtocol: The cultured cells were processed for bottom-up proteomics. The cells were lysed, reduced with dithiothreitol, alkylated with iodoacetamide, and the extracted proteins were purified via precipitation (acetone, –20 ºC, overnight). The protein pellets were reconstructed in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, followed by tryptic digestion (1:50 protein:protease ratio, 37 ºC, 12 h, overnight). The resulting peptides were barcoded using isobaric tandem mass tags following a TMT10plex reagent (Lot no. SG253269, Thermo Scientific). The labeling channels were randomized across phenotypes. Each phenotype was measured in n = 5 biological replicates (BRs, BR1–5). The schema of labeling was as follows: Nt (129N), La (131), Pg (126), AppNt (128N), AppLa (130N), and AppPg (127N) for BR1; Nt (128), La (129N), Pg (127N), AppNt (131), AppLa (126), and AppPg (130N) for BR2; Nt (131), La (126), Pg (129N), AppNt (128N), AppLa (127N), and AppPg (130N) for BR3; Nt (127N), La (130N), Pg (129N), AppNt (131), AppLa (126), AppPg (128N) for BR4; Nt (130N), La (128N), Pg (127N), AppNt (126), AppLa (131), and AppPg (129N) for BR5. The tagged peptides were mixed in an equal total peptide ratio. The mixture was fractionated using high pH reversed-phase liquid chromatography (LC), and the fractions were concatenated into 8 fractions based on orthogonality. Each fraction was separated at low pH on a micropillar array column (µPAC) using reversed-phase nanoLC. The separated peptides were ionized in a nano-electrospray ionization source (stainless steel emitter, product no. ES542, Thermo Scientific; spray potential, +2,300 V). The ionized peptides were detected on a tribrid (orbitrap-quadrupole-ion trap) high-resolution mass spectrometer (Orbitrap Fusion Lumos, Thermo). The survey (MS1) spectra were collected at 120,000 FWHM resolution in the orbitrap analyzer (max IT, auto; AGC threshold, 5×103 counts). The peptide signals were selected for MS2 fragmentation in the CID cell containing helium via data-dependent acquisition (dynamic exclusion, 60 s): collision energy, 35% NCE; max IT, auto; AGC, standard. The top 10 MS2 fragments were selected for multi-notched MS3 fragmentation in the HCD cell in nitrogen: collision energy, 55% NCE; analyzer, orbitrap (15,000 FWMH resolution); max IT, auto; AGC, 300% normalized
dataProcessingProtocol: The MS files were analyzed in Proteome Discoverer 2.2 (for proteomics) or 3.0 (for phosphoproteomics) against the UniProt Homo Sapiens proteome (20,380 genes, downloaded on 6/8/2021) using SEQUEST-HT. The search settings were: methionine oxidation, variable; N-terminus acetylation, dynamic; carbamidomethylation on cysteine, fixed; lysine TMT10plex, fixed; max missed cleavage, 2; precursor mass tolerance, 10 ppm; fragment mass tolerance, 0.6 Da. The peptides and proteins were filtered to < 1% FDR, determined against the reversed-sequence decoy. Protein identification and quantification were based on detecting at least 1 proteotypic peptide. The measured reporter ion signal abundance was used as a proxy for protein concentration.
